correctness.rationale: For each voter the strict-copy attacker score is the quadratic integral of the squared relative-rank coordinate. Three-draw self-play fixes the minimax bound at 1/3 and makes all supported scores tight. Positive definite Hessian implies uniqueness. If strict Condorcet winner B is excluded, pure A and pure C fail because B beats either in more than half the votes; positive A,C support forces t=3(u+m)-1 and the exact remaining B-score inequality. Conversely that inequality gives all three scores <=1/3. Direct substitutions establish the three symmetric branches and their exact transition values 1/3 and 4/9; proof handles all finite electorate sizes, not just tested rational grid. Exact script output: 10788 and 1866 comparisons.

value.rationale: An exact necessary-and-sufficient exclusion region for a strict Condorcet winner is a natural structural invariant of an influential two-draw randomized voting rule under the canonical single-peaked preference restriction. The general criterion depends on the four ranking frequencies and identifies a robust open exclusion region (e.g. p=9/20), and its symmetric cross-section has two distinct sharp support changes at p=1/3 and p=4/9. This distinguishes two-draw stability from pairwise-majority responsiveness beyond the previously implicit single tuned boundary witness; it is a genuine complete classification on a motivated preference domain, not a grid calculation or a restatement of existing uniqueness.
